title: An embedded strict-transform resolution is an ordinary labeled tower
statement: Let L be a linearly ordered label type and S a reduced finite-type rational scheme [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]. Let p be a permitted embedding of S [def-trf-intrinsic-labeled-resolution], and let T be a labeled embedded resolution tower of p [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. There exists an intrinsic labeled ordinary tower A on S, together with an identification of its entire cut diagram, initial map, labels and center ideals with the intrinsic diagram of T [def-trf-intrinsic-labeled-resolution]. No smooth comparison or global assignment is asserted.

source.place: VIII 2.1.1--2.1.9, 2.3.1, 2.3.4--2.3.5, 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.86--88,91--94. Agent expansion of the conditional embedded-to-intrinsic argument, not a separately quoted ILO theorem.

proof.text: Enumerate the finite set of labels of T in increasing order, with length n. For i<n take the intrinsic level just before the ith label; take the top cut as the last level. Transport the initial isomorphism through p. Let index(s) count the active labels in s. Its monotonicity, endpoints, and values at the before cuts follow from the increasing enumeration. Use T.constantIntrinsic between cuts with equal sets of labels to identify every cut with its numbered ordinary level. Functoriality gives transition laws and stage_naturality.

At each active label the ambient center factors through the current strict transform as a closed immersion. Thus the ideal of this closed subscheme is the ambient center ideal extended to the strict transform. The strict-transform/blowup identification [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed], realized by exists_blowup_comap_iso_strictTransform in the same source module, makes the next level its ordinary blowup, compatibly with the transition. This supplies blowupIso and blowup_fac. Define the intrinsic cut center as the kernel of centerToIntrinsic; its coherence, nonempty support, nowhere density and regular subscheme follow from the supplied fields of T. At an absent label the subscheme is empty and its ideal is the unit ideal.

The final level is regular by finalRegular. regularInput and emptyInput make the label set empty, hence the length zero, in their respective cases. Keep T.intrinsic itself as the cut diagram. Its identity natural isomorphism gives the identification with T, with the specified initial map, labels, and actual center ideals. Empty label sets need no exceptional case beyond n=0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ordinary_tower_of_embedded
    {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L] (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u})
    (p : RationalResolutionEmbedding S) (T : LabeledEmbeddedResolutionTower L p.pair) :
    ∃ A : IntrinsicLabeledOrdinaryTower L S.scheme,
      Nonempty (IntrinsicEmbeddedResolutionIdentification A p T)
